coalition_name: New Mexico Coalition Against Domestic Violence
criminal_definition: Knowingly pursuing a pattern of conduct that would cause a reasonable person to feel frightened, intimidated, or threatened, intending to place the victim in reasonable apprehension of death, bodily harm, sexual assault, confinement, or restraint, or to cause fear for the victim's or a household member's safety.
criminal_penalty: Stalking: misdemeanor, up to 364 days in jail and/or up to $1,000 fine; second or subsequent conviction: fourth-degree felony; aggravated stalking (NMSA 1978, § 30-3A-3.1): fourth-degree felony, second conviction third-degree felony.
cyber_note: Harassment includes a pattern of conduct with an electronic communication device intended to seriously alarm or terrorize, and stalking under § 30-3A-3 includes remote surveillance by an electronic communication device.
order_duration: For a fixed period of any length the court finds appropriate to protect the victim; the order may be extended.
order_free_note: No filing, issuance, or service fees are charged for a petition for an order of protection.
order_where: District Court in the county where the victim resides; stalking is defined as domestic abuse under the Act whether or not the stalker is a household member

coalition_name: New York State Coalition Against Domestic Violence
criminal_definition: Intentionally and repeatedly following, monitoring (in person or electronically), or engaging in a course of conduct toward another person, knowing or having reason to know it is likely to cause fear of material harm to physical, mental, or emotional health, or fear of suicide or self-inflicted injury.
criminal_penalty: Stalking in the fourth degree: Class B misdemeanor; third degree: Class A misdemeanor; second degree: Class E felony, up to 4 years in prison; first degree: Class D felony, up to 7 years in prison.
cyber_note: New York has no separate cyberstalking statute; stalking under Penal Law § 120.45 expressly includes following or monitoring by electronic means.
order_duration: Up to 8 years from sentencing for a felony conviction, 5 years for a Class A misdemeanor, and 2 years for any other offense.
order_gap_note: New York has no standalone civil stalking order a victim files on their own — protection comes through the criminal case: the order is issued by the criminal court handling the stalking case or at sentencing.
order_name: Order of Protection under Criminal Procedure Law § 530.13
order_where: The criminal court handling the stalking case (Criminal Court, Supreme Court, or local court where the criminal action is pending); New York has no standalone civil stalking order a victim files on their own — protection comes through the criminal case

coalition_name: North Carolina Coalition Against Domestic Violence
criminal_definition: Willfully and repeatedly harassing another person, or engaging in a course of conduct without legal purpose, knowing or having reason to know it would cause a reasonable person to fear for their safety or suffer substantial emotional distress.
criminal_penalty: First offense: Class A1 misdemeanor, up to 150 days in jail; repeat offense: Class F felony; stalking while a court order prohibiting the conduct is in effect: Class H felony.
cyber_note: Cyberstalking covers using email or other electronic communication to threaten bodily harm or property damage, or to repeatedly communicate to abuse, annoy, threaten, terrify, or harass; a Class 2 misdemeanor.
order_duration: A permanent order lasts for a fixed period of up to one year.
order_free_note: No court costs or fees are charged for filing or serving the complaint and orders under N.C. Gen. Stat. § 50C-2.
order_where: District Court, filed through the Clerk of Superior Court in the county where the case is filed

coalition_name: CAWS North Dakota (North Dakota Council on Abused Women's Services)
criminal_definition: Intentionally engaging in a course of conduct directed at a specific person that frightens, intimidates, or harasses them and serves no legitimate purpose, or unauthorized tracking of a person's movements or location by GPS or other electronic means.
criminal_penalty: Class A misdemeanor (up to 360 days in jail, up to $3,000 fine); Class C felony (up to 5 years in prison, up to $10,000 fine) if the offender has a prior conviction for certain offenses against the victim or the stalking violates a court protection order.
cyber_note: Stalking includes unauthorized tracking of a person's movements or location by GPS or other electronic means, and harassment under N.D.C.C. § 12.1-17-07 covers threats and repeated contact by electronic communication.
order_where: District Court in the county where the victim lives

criminal_definition: Engaging in a pattern of conduct (two or more actions or incidents closely related in time) that knowingly causes another person to believe the offender will cause physical harm to them or a family or household member, or cause mental distress.
criminal_penalty: First offense: first-degree misdemeanor, up to 180 days in jail and/or up to $1,000 fine; fourth-degree felony (6 to 18 months in prison, up to $5,000 fine) if the offender has a prior menacing-by-stalking conviction or another aggravating factor applies.
order_where: Court of Common Pleas in the county where the victim lives

coalition_name: Oklahoma Coalition Against Domestic Violence and Sexual Assault
criminal_definition: Willfully, maliciously, and repeatedly following or harassing another person in a manner that would cause a reasonable person (or a member of their immediate family) to feel frightened, intimidated, threatened, harassed, or molested, and that actually causes the victim to feel that way.
criminal_penalty: First offense: misdemeanor, up to 1 year in jail and/or up to $1,000 fine; stalking while a protective order is in effect or a repeat offense: felony, up to 5 years; a second act of stalking within 10 years of a prior stalking conviction: felony, up to 20 years and/or up to $25,000 fine.
order_duration: Up to five years; a continuous order is possible in certain cases, such as a prior felony stalking conviction or a history of violating court orders.
order_free_note: No filing fee, service fee, attorney fee, or other fee or cost is charged to the victim for filing a petition for a protective order.
order_where: District Court in the county where the victim resides, the defendant resides, or the violence occurred

coalition_name: Oregon Coalition Against Domestic and Sexual Violence
criminal_definition: Knowingly alarming or coercing another person or a member of their immediate family or household by engaging in repeated and unwanted contact, where it is objectively reasonable for the victim to be alarmed or coerced and the contact causes the victim reasonable apprehension for their personal safety.
criminal_penalty: Class A misdemeanor (up to 364 days in jail); Class B felony if the person has a prior stalking conviction, is subject to an active protection order, or at least one instance of unwanted contact was a felony, unlawful dissemination of an intimate image, or unlawful use of a GPS device.
cyber_note: Oregon has no separate cyberstalking charge; online and electronic communications can qualify as stalking under ORS 163.732.
order_duration: Unlimited duration unless limited by law or court order.
order_where: Circuit Court — file a civil petition directly with the court, or start the process by filing a complaint with a law enforcement officer, who issues a citation ordering the respondent to appear in court within three judicial days

criminal_definition: Engaging in a course of conduct or repeatedly committing acts toward another person, including following without proper authority, or repeatedly communicating with another person, under circumstances showing an intent to place that person in reasonable fear of bodily injury or to cause substantial emotional distress.
criminal_penalty: First offense: misdemeanor of the first degree; second or subsequent offense, or a first offense after a prior conviction for a crime of violence against the same victim or family or household member: felony of the third degree.
order_free_note: There is no cost to file for a protection order.
order_gap_note: Pennsylvania has no general civil stalking order for adult victims — the Protection From Sexual Violence (SVP) order covers stalking only if it involved a sexual offense, and the Protection From Intimidation (PFI) order covers only a minor victim stalked or harassed by an adult. An adult stalking victim with no sexual offense has no ch. 62A order available.
order_name: Protection From Sexual Violence (SVP) order (only if the stalking involved a sexual offense) or Protection From Intimidation (PFI) order (only for a minor victim stalked or harassed by an adult); Pennsylvania has no general civil stalking order for adult victims
order_where: Court of Common Pleas at the county courthouse where the victim lives

coalition_name: Rhode Island Coalition Against Domestic Violence
criminal_definition: Willfully, maliciously, and repeatedly following or harassing another person with the intent to place that person in reasonable fear of bodily injury, or harassing another person.
criminal_penalty: Felony, up to 5 years in prison and/or up to $10,000 fine.
cyber_note: Cyberstalking and cyberharassment covers transmitting communications by computer or other electronic device for the sole purpose of harassing a person or their family; first offense is a misdemeanor (up to 1 year, up to $500 fine), and a second or subsequent conviction is a felony (up to 2 years, up to $6,000 fine).
order_duration: A final order lasts for a fixed period of up to three years and may be extended.
order_where: District Court in the county where the victim lives; a temporary order can be issued the same day the complaint is filed

coalition_name: South Carolina Coalition Against Domestic Violence and Sexual Assault
criminal_definition: A pattern of words or conduct, whether verbal, written, or electronic, that serves no legitimate purpose and is intended to cause, and does cause, a targeted person (and would cause a reasonable person) to fear death, assault, bodily injury, criminal sexual contact, kidnapping, or property damage to the person or a family member.
criminal_penalty: Felony: first offense up to 5 years in prison and/or up to $5,000 fine; up to 10 years and/or up to $7,000 fine if a restraining order or injunction was in effect; up to 15 years and/or up to $10,000 fine with a prior harassment or stalking conviction within 10 years.
cyber_note: Stalking expressly includes a pattern of words or conduct, whether verbal, written, or electronic, that causes reasonable fear of harm.
order_duration: A fixed period of not less than one year, as determined by the court; the order may be extended for good cause.
order_free_note: A $55 filing fee is assessed to the non-prevailing party.
order_where: Magistrates Court in the county where the defendant resides, where the harassment or stalking occurred, or where the plaintiff resides if the defendant is a nonresident or cannot be found
